how: Repeated calls recruit helpers for several figures and companions rather than one exclusive project.

statement: explaining the canvas to participants and latecomers
how: Members explain both the live pixel canvas and its finalized state to people who missed the event.
A member claims to have started the original figure while asking helpers to add its companion.
Success announcements, a companion in progress and repair reports make the work's state public.
Participants debate references, colours and alterations while contesting what still counts as their character.
Writing the subreddit name on the beam is proposed both as a signature and as a replacement for vandalism.
A reference image and an instruction to keep to one version offer shared targets without demonstrating universal assent.
A dissenter abandons one design fight for lack of support and redirects effort to repairs while accepting compromise.
Template instructions settle a version only among accepting participants, since reported approval coexists with conflicting corrections and rejected alterations.
Calls and work reports establish participation opportunities and sequence without identifying which call caused particular placements.
The claimed starter combines an origin claim with a concrete request for helpers in the same passage.
Requests to consolidate divided effort do not establish an absolute judgement of too few hands or too little space.
Short repair reports and thanks are visible, but these coded passages do not establish a bare acceptance of a preceding recruitment call.
The coded recruitment exchange contains a report of earlier repair rather than a demonstrated bare answer accepting its new build proposal.
Public requests for organisation and an unseen chat leave both hidden decided order and the global numerical claim beyond this room's test.
Repair pressure and communication with a chat do not establish adoption or rejection of placement automation.
Members defend existing work, report persistent healing and put repair ahead of extending the beam.
The success announcement immediately directs defenders to hold the finished work.
Concentrating effort requires choosing between figures, ordering repair before extension and recommending a more stable location for a companion.
Repairing together requires enough agreement about the target image to avoid participants undoing one another's corrections.
Participants contest attack authorship, attribute damage to disguised rivals and deny responsibility for a beam they cannot control.
Attributions and denials remain participant accounts unless independent evidence identifies the placers responsible.
A suggestion to build beside stable figures cannot establish an actual move following loss of the original spot.
The relocation suggestion supplies neither a demonstrated loss-driven move nor a preceding judgement that the room lacks enough hands.
A repairer's shortage of spare pixels does not establish whether upkeep prompted placement automation outside the visible account.
Neighbours negotiate beam routes, shared colours, coexistence and coordinated changes around existing art.
Representatives exchange a restoration offer, nonaggression and an explicit acceptance carried to a chat.
Members propose avoiding neighbouring art and visitors ask that small logos and a rival character be spared.
Members oppose an attack by invoking nonaggression and the existing alliance.
Offers trade defensive help for shared space and promise to repel a common attacker for both works.
Thanks, a help question and a greeting instantiate reciprocity's smaller forms without establishing a treaty for every contact.
An existing alliance is celebrated and a further alliance is publicly announced.
A self-described negotiator proposes peace and another representative relays nonaggression to a chat.
Negotiating restraint may first require separating an apparent attack by the room's artwork from responsibility of the people negotiating.
A speaker can offer beam correction only when repair commitments leave pixels available to enact it.
A protection-for-restoration offer is answered with nonaggression while the responder explicitly prioritises defence.
An alliance supplies the explicit reason for objecting to a proposed attack.
A proposed merge receives a conditional defensive-help bargain rather than an unconditional assent.
Restoration and protection are exchanged as offers, while their delivery and any common shortage of hands require separate evidence.
Public alliance announcements establish cooperation claims while their effectiveness against all attackers remains a participant's account.
Claims to represent most members and denials of beam control do not establish an explicit dispute over who may commit the room to a treaty.
The ceasefire exchange and later denial of control cannot establish that negotiating a treaty caused a dispute over authority to bind placers.
Coexistence and contested alterations do not demonstrate a host ruling over another room's work as its guest.
Familiar characters and lore supply the content of proposed works without identifying a preexisting quarrel with the attack targets.
The attack appeals name targets but contain no evidence that a prior community quarrel was carried onto the canvas.
Fandom references and rival-directed attack calls do not establish a pre-canvas tie naming the rival in the attack turn.
The unplaced April Fools theme fits a separate fandom takeover joke alongside serious canvas recruitment.
Members request flair and object to event posts burying ordinary discussion without demonstrating that moderators enacted a new rule.
A member explicitly explains the flair request by the flood of canvas threads burying ordinary posts.
The final work is celebrated as an accomplishment while the same reflection preserves disagreement over an alteration.
A successful mark is publicly announced and immediately made an object of defence.
Dismay, complaint and consolation report contrasting assessments of the finished work rather than a shared change of mind.
A recruitment title invites character making on a successor canvas without establishing that participants actually continued there.
The success announcement combines reporting completion and publicly marking it in a single turn.
Celebration and later appraisals do not supply a passage showing that marking success prompted preservation of a record.
The successor-canvas invitation follows finished-canvas accounts but does not identify remembrance as its motive.
Complaints about the final design do not identify a shared cleanup copy or an explicit contest over which historical record to preserve.
Participants call for destroying rival work and promise public heroism for an attack.
A title claims the destruction of rival work as a victory in talk.
Recruitment and attack proposals do not establish room control of an offensive when members deny responsibility and control of the depicted beam.
The attack appeal receives an explicit objection explaining that the target is an ally.
A proposed attack is checked by invoking the existing alliance in the immediate reply.
A destruction call and later victory title show contest talk without proving which placers acted or that the call caused the claimed result.
